initialUserIntent: One of the project goals is to realize IntelliJ-Ultimate-class multi-language features. The updated RefactorKit (0.7.0, repo cdadcbb3) now runtime-supports Kotlin (kotlin-compiler K2) with definition/references/symbols. For the newly available languages, prepare the supporting features (syntax highlighting) IN ADDITION to RefactorKit's own features. This slice covers Kotlin: (a) supporting feature — Kotlin syntax highlighting in the editor (.kt/.kts -> Monaco built-in Kotlin tokenizer via the monacoLanguage extension/alias map); (b) RefactorKit feature — Kotlin navigation (go-to-definition, find-references, document/workspace symbols) via the engine kotlin commands (refactorkit kotlin definition/references/symbols, position-based --file/--line/--character, toolchain-qualified --jdk-home/--compiler-jar), with honest-unavailable when the Kotlin toolchain or capability is absent.

requirement.title: Kotlin syntax highlighting and navigation wired in the IDE
requirement.classification: Story BDD + Spec BDD for pure view-model decisions
requirement.capability: Kotlin supporting feature (syntax highlighting) + RefactorKit navigation (go-to-definition, find-references, symbols). (a) monacoLanguage.ts maps .kt/.kts and language kotlin to the Monaco built-in Kotlin language so the editor highlights Kotlin. (b) The IDE resolves a Kotlin symbol definition and references via the RefactorKit engine kotlin commands (position-based, toolchain-qualified), presents them, and navigates/reveals the selected location in the editor (reusing documentNavigation.navigateToLocation + editor.revealRequest). Honest-unavailable when the Kotlin toolchain or capability is absent. Kotlin refactoring is a separate later slice.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: A Kotlin document (.kt/.kts or language kotlin) resolves to the Monaco Kotlin language and receives syntax highlighting (not plaintext).
Given a Kotlin position (file/line/character) and the Kotlin toolchain, the IDE resolves go-to-definition via the engine kotlin definition command and reveals the location in the editor.
Given a Kotlin position, the IDE resolves find-references via the engine kotlin references command, presents them, and navigating/reveals a selected reference.
The flow follows extract -> delegate -> response with no hidden domain policy; absent Kotlin toolchain or capability reports honest unavailable/error, never fabricated result.
Boundary invariant: packages/ui, packages/web-core, apps/web never import @tauri-apps/api; browser/Tauri Kotlin implementations live behind frontend ports.
Status is evidence-based with an explicit state, never inferred from shells; live Tauri-window Kotlin navigation E2E may remain unvalidated if headless (recorded honestly).
